newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND MAY LIFT BANKS' OBLIGATORY RESERVES IN '97.
newsitem.headline: POLAND MAY LIFT BANKS' OBLIGATORY RESERVES IN '97.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, is considering lifting banks' obligatory reserve requirements next year, the NBP's deputy president said on Saturday.

"It seems to me the banking crisis is subsiding -- fewer banks have failed lately. If everything continues in that direction, next year we can do something to take a burden off banks -- I have in mind freeing banks from the burden of obligatory reserves," Witold Kozinski said.
Kozinski made the comment at a meeting commemorating the first cooperative bank in Poland 135 years ago. The country currently has 1,500 such banks.

Obligatory reserves, currently at 17 percent and nine percent for zloty call and term deposits respectively, were deemed necessary after several banks failed early in the decade when Poland was beginning its change to a market economy.
The Polish Banking Association (ZBP) and Banking Guarantee Fund (BFG) have recently been lobbying for their reduction.
